definition_zh: 生物碱；（尤指植物中的）含氮碱性有机化合物
definition_en: a nitrogen-containing organic compound of plant origin that usually has marked physiological action on the body
core_image: 藏在植物里的苦味药性分子：一口咬下去又苦又冲
scene: 药学课上老师切开一种有毒的植物果实。The scientist extracted a bitter alkaloid from the plant.
sceneCN: 这里的 alkaloid 是「生物碱」（第 1 个义项：从植物中提取的含氮碱性化合物）；句意是科学家从植物中提取出一种苦味的生物碱。

pos.zh: 生物碱；含氮碱性有机化合物

derivatives.zh: 同族形容词，义为「碱性的」，与 alkali 相关
同族名词，义为「碱」，是 alkaloid 的直接来源
由 alkali 加动词后缀构成，义为「碱化」

senses.title: A nitrogenous plant compound with drug-like action
senses.titleCN: 生物碱：植物含氮碱性化合物
senses.definition: an organic, nitrogen-containing compound made by plants that strongly affects animal bodies
senses.definitionCN: 植物产生的含氮有机化合物，对动物机体有强烈作用
senses.example: Morphine is an alkaloid obtained from the opium poppy.
senses.exampleCN: 吗啡是从罂粟中提取的一种生物碱。
senses.why: The word is built on alkali plus -oid, so the core image is an alkali-like substance hiding in plants.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 alkali（碱）加 -oid（类似物）构成，核心意象是藏在植物里的类似碱的物质。

senses.title: Any synthetic compound resembling plant alkaloids
senses.titleCN: 类生物碱：人工合成的相似化合物
senses.definition: a synthetic or semisynthetic compound whose structure or action resembles natural plant alkaloids
senses.definitionCN: 结构或作用类似天然植物生物碱的合成或半合成化合物
senses.example: The lab produced a synthetic alkaloid for pain relief.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室合成了一种用于镇痛的类生物碱。
senses.why: Once the natural class was named, chemistry extended -oid to any look-alike compound.
senses.whyCN: 天然类别命名后，化学界把 -oid（类似）扩展到任何外观相似的化合物上。

senses.title: Alkaloids collectively as a class
senses.titleCN: 生物碱类：作为整体类别
senses.definition: alkaloids considered collectively as a chemical family in pharmacology
senses.definitionCN: 药理学中作为一族化学物质被整体谈论的生物碱
senses.example: This family of alkaloids affects the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 这一族生物碱作用于神经系统。
senses.why: A mass sense arises when chemists talk about the family rather than one compound.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家谈论整个家族而非单个化合物时，就产生了不可数的类指义项。

senses.title: A specific alkaloid molecule identified in analysis
senses.definition: a particular alkaloid identified or measured in chemical analysis
senses.definitionCN: 化学分析中被鉴定或测出的某一种生物碱
senses.example: Each alkaloid was separated by chromatography.
senses.exampleCN: 每种生物碱都通过色谱法被分离出来。
senses.why: The countable sense lets researchers point at one molecule within the family.
senses.whyCN: 可数义项让研究者能指向家族中的某一个分子。

senses.title: A poisonous principle in toxicology
senses.definition: an alkaloid regarded as the toxic principle of a poisonous plant
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有毒植物毒性来源的生物碱成分
senses.example: The poison actsonally through its alkaloid.
senses.exampleCN: 这种毒物实际上是靠其中的生物碱起作用的。
senses.why: Because many alkaloids are bitter and toxic, toxicology singles them out as the active poison.
senses.whyCN: 许多生物碱苦而有毒，毒理学因此把它们单独看作起效的毒物成分。

senses.title: An alkaloid used as medicine
senses.definition: an alkaloid used as a pharmacologically active ingredient in drugs
senses.definitionCN: 用作药物中有效成分的生物碱
senses.example: Doctors prescribed an alkaloid to lower blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了一种降压的生物碱类药物。
senses.why: The same strong action that makes alkaloids toxic makes them valuable medicines.
senses.whyCN: 让生物碱有毒的那种强烈作用，也正是它们能入药的原因。

senses.title: Alkaloid content of a material
senses.definition: the amount of alkaloids present in a plant or product, measured as a proportion
senses.definitionCN: 植物或产品中所含生物碱的量，以比例计
senses.example: This variety has a high alkaloid content.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品种的生物碱含量很高。
senses.why: In agriculture and industry the word shifts from naming a molecule to naming an amount.
senses.whyCN: 在农业和工业语境中，这个词从指称分子转为指称含量。

senses.title: A marker for plant classification
senses.definition: the alkaloid profile of a plant used to identify or classify the species
senses.definitionCN: 用于鉴定或分类物种的植物生物碱谱
senses.example: Researchers compared the alkaloid profile of two related species.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者比较了两个近缘种的生物碱谱。
senses.why: Because each species makes its own alkaloid mixture, the mixture becomes a fingerprint.
senses.whyCN: 每个物种产生自己独特的生物碱混合物，这种混合物就成了指纹。

intro.en: Alkaloid combines alkali with the adjective suffix -oid, coined in early nineteenth-century chemistry.
intro.cn: alkaloid 由 alkali（碱）加形容词后缀 -oid（类似……的）构成，是十九世纪早期化学的造词。

items.en: al-qalya, "the ashes of saltwort", the source of alkali.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qalya「盐蓬草的灰烬」，是 alkali 的来源。

items.en: alkali, borrowed from Arabic for the caustic ash substance.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alkali，借自阿拉伯语，指苛性灰质。

items.en: -oides, "like, resembling", adapted into Latin as -oid.
items.cn: 希腊语 -oides「类似」，经拉丁语转为 -oid。

items.en: German Chemists formed Alkaloid for the alkali-like plant bases.
items.cn: 十九世纪一二十年代德国化学家造 Alkaloid 一词指碱性的植物碱类。

items.en: English alkaloid appears in chemical writing soon after.
items.cn: 英语 alkaloid 随后在化学文献中出现。

items.en: Now the standard pharmacological term for nitrogenous plant bases.
items.cn: 如今是药理学中含氮植物碱的标准术语。

note.en: Distinguish alkaloid from its sibling words alkali and alkaline, and from look-alike chemistry terms.
note.cn: 要把 alkaloid 与同族词 alkali、alkaline 区分开，也要与拼写相近的化学词区分。

entries.definition: a soluble base such as lye; the parent word of alkaloid.
entries.definitionCN: 碱（如碱液）；alkaloid 的来源词。

entries.definition: adjective meaning containing or like an alkali.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「碱性的」，与 alkali 同根。

entries.definition: a different class of organic compounds; shares the Arabic al- article but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 另一类有机化合物；同样带有阿拉伯语冠词 al-，但词根不同，只是形近。

entries.definition: another class of plant-derived bioactive compounds, built on sugars.
entries.definitionCN: 另一类植物来源的活性化合物，以糖为骨架。

entries.definition: a bitter plant compound that precipitates proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 使蛋白质沉淀的苦味植物化合物。

entries.definition: any poisonous substance, of which some alkaloids are examples.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指有毒物质，部分生物碱属于毒素。

normalIntro.en: Remember alkaloid through its two building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 通过两个构件记住 alkaloid。

normal.en: alkali + -oid: an alkali-like substance.
normal.cn: alkali（碱）+ -oid（类似物）：像碱一样的物质。

normal.en: al-qalya was the ash of saltwort plants — alkaloids often come from plants too.
normal.cn: al-qalya 原指盐蓬草灰烬——生物碱也常来自植物。

normal.en: Family chain: alkali → alkaline → alkaloid, from base to adjective to plant molecule.
normal.cn: 词族链条：alkali → alkaline → alkaloid，从碱到形容词再到植物分子。

normal.en: Most alkaloids are bitter — think of the -oid ending as "the bitter look-alike".
normal.cn: 多数生物碱是苦的——把 -oid 想成「苦味的类似物」。

normal.en: Morphine, caffeine, nicotine: famous -oid-less members, all alkaloids.
normal.cn: 吗啡、咖啡因、尼古丁：虽然没有 -oid 结尾，都是著名生物碱。

abstract.en: Picture a green leaf hiding a tiny crystal of "plant alkali".
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿叶里藏着一粒「植物碱」的小晶体。

abstract.en: The bitter taste on your tongue is the molecule announcing itself.
abstract.cn: 舌尖的苦味就是分子在自我通报。

abstract.en: A chemist ladles ash from a plant fire and pulls out a white powder.
abstract.cn: 化学家从烧尽的植物灰里舀出一勺白色粉末。

examples.en: Caffeine is the best-known alkaloid in tea and coffee.
examples.cn: 咖啡因是茶和咖啡中最著名的生物碱。

examples.en: The alkaloid content of the herb makes it toxic to livestock.
examples.cn: 这种草药的生物碱含量使它对牲畜有毒。

examples.en: Chemists isolated a new alkaloid from the rainforest vine.
examples.cn: 化学家从雨林藤蔓中分离出一种新的生物碱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥克劳德」——想想“苦味的老克劳德”，他像碱一样冲口，是从植物里熬出来的老药汤。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-qalya（盐蓬草的灰烬，制碱原料）经中世纪拉丁语 alkali 进入英语，十九世纪化学家加上希腊语来源的 -oid（类似）构成 alkaloid，字面义为「类似碱的物质」。

sensesIntro.en: From the basic chemical class, the senses widen to synthetic look-alikes, the family as a whole, single molecules, and then to poison, medicine, content, and classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 从基本的化学类别出发，义项扩展到合成的类似物、作为整体的家族、单个分子，再到毒物、药物、含量和分类用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bitter alkali-like molecule hidden in plants
core.cn: 核心意象：藏在植物里的苦味类碱分子

branches.en: The basic nitrogenous plant compound itself.
branches.cn: 基本的含氮植物化合物本身。

branches.en: Synthetic look-alikes and the family considered collectively.
branches.cn: 合成的类似物与作为整体谈论的家族。

branches.en: Single molecules, whether as poison or analyzed substance.
branches.cn: 单个分子，无论作为毒物还是分析对象。

branches.en: The same strong action turned into medicine.
branches.cn: 同样的强烈作用转化为药物。

branches.en: Content and profile as practical measures and markers.
branches.cn: 含量与谱系作为实用指标和分类标记。

intro.en: Alkaloid is transparently built from a borrowed base and a Greek-derived suffix.
intro.cn: alkaloid 由借来的词基和希腊来源的后缀清晰构成。

latinIntro.en: The root traveled from Arabic through Medieval Latin into European chemistry.
latinIntro.cn: 词根经阿拉伯语和中世纪拉丁语进入欧洲化学。

definition_zh: 减轻；缓和；平息（恐惧、怀疑、疼痛等）
definition_en: to reduce the intensity of a fear, doubt, pain, or other unpleasant feeling
core_image: 把烧得正旺的火苗轻轻压灭
scene: 洪水退去后村民仍在发抖。The mayor spoke calmly to allay their fears.
sceneCN: 这里的 allay 是「平息、减轻」（第 1 个义项：减轻不安情绪）；句意是镇长平静地讲话以平息村民的恐惧。

derivatives.zh: 罕用派生词，义为「减轻；平息」
同根基础动词，义为「放平；放置」

senses.title: To reduce fear or worry
senses.definition: to make a fear or worry less strong
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧或担忧变得不那么强烈
senses.example: The report allayed public fears about the vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告打消了公众对疫苗的恐惧。
senses.why: The core image is laying something down; a fear is pressed flat until it calms.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「放平」；恐惧被压平、按下去，直到平息。

senses.title: To dispel doubt or suspicion
senses.definition: to remove doubt or suspicion by giving reassurance or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过安抚或举证除去怀疑
senses.example: She produced receipts to allay their suspicions.
senses.exampleCN: 她出示收据以消除他们的怀疑。
senses.why: Suspicion, like fear, is an unrested state that can be laid to rest.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑和恐惧一样是不安的状态，可以被「安放」下来。

senses.title: To lessen pain or hunger
senses.definition: to ease physical discomfort such as pain, hunger, or thirst
senses.definitionCN: 缓解疼痛、饥饿或口渴等身体不适
senses.example: A hot meal allayed their hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭缓解了他们的饥饿。
senses.why: Physical distress is another kind of inner turbulence that settles when laid low.
senses.whyCN: 身体的不适是另一种内在骚动，被压下去就安定了。

senses.title: To quiet anger or conflict
senses.definition: to calm anger or bring an angry situation under control
senses.definitionCN: 使怒气平息或控制住愤怒的局面
senses.example: His apology allayed her anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉平息了她的怒气。
senses.why: Anger is pictured as a flame; allaying is smothering the fire down.
senses.whyCN: 怒气被比作火焰；allay 就是把火压熄。

senses.title: To calm a disturbance or unrest
senses.definition: to restore calm to a disturbed situation, crowd, or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 使骚动的局面、人群或气氛恢复平静
senses.example: Police moved in to allay the unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 警方介入以平定骚乱。
senses.why: The image of laying things flat extends from feelings to whole situations.
senses.whyCN: 「放平」的意象从情绪扩展到整个局势。

senses.title: To moderate intensity gradually
senses.definition: to cause something intense to weaken by degrees rather than vanish at once
senses.definitionCN: 使强烈的事物逐步减弱而非立刻消失
senses.example: Time allayed the grief little by little.
senses.exampleCN: 时间一点点减轻了悲伤。
senses.why: Laying something down is gradual; the verb suggests slow settling, not instant removal.
senses.whyCN: 放平是渐进的动作；这个词暗示缓慢平复，而非瞬间消除。

senses.title: To ease another person by one's actions
senses.definition: to reassure someone through words or deeds so their unease subsides
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或行动安抚某人使其不安消退
senses.example: The captain walked the deck to allay the passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在甲板上巡视以安抚乘客。
senses.why: The verb can act directly on people, not only on their feelings.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以直接作用于人，而不仅限于情绪本身。

senses.title: Archaic: to lay or put to rest
senses.definition: in older use, to lay something down physically or put it to rest
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法：把某物放下或使其安息
senses.example: Old texts speak of allaying a body in the tomb.
senses.exampleCN: 古文本中有将遗体安放于墓中的说法。
senses.why: This preserves the original physical sense before the emotional one took over.
senses.whyCN: 这保留了最初的物理义，后来情感义才占主导。

intro.en: Allay descends from Old English lecgan "to lay", with the prefix a- absorbed from the verb phrase.
intro.cn: allay 源自古英语 lecgan「放平」，前缀 a- 来自动词短语的合并。

items.en: Reconstructed root *lagjan, "to lay, set down".
items.cn: 重构词根 *lagjan「放、置」。

items.en: alecgan, "to lay down, put away, diminish".
items.cn: 古英语 alecgan「放平、搁置、减少」。

items.en: alayen, the sense narrowing toward calming feelings.
items.cn: 中古英语 alayen，词义向平息情绪收窄。

items.en: allay fixed in the sense of easing fear, pain, hunger.
items.cn: allay 固定为减轻恐惧、疼痛、饥饿之义。

items.en: Widely used by Shakespeare-era writers.
items.cn: 莎士比亚时代作家广泛使用。

items.en: Now chiefly formal, reserved for feelings and appetites.
items.cn: 如今主要用于正式语体，限于情绪与欲求。

note.en: Allay is often confused with alley in sound, and with its near synonyms relieve and alleviate in meaning.
note.cn: allay 在发音上常与 alley 混淆，在意义上与近义词 relieve、alleviate 相近。

entries.definition: a narrow street or lane; only similar in sound, completely different root.
entries.definitionCN: 小巷、胡同；只是发音相近，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: a mixture of metals; resembles allay in spelling but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 合金；拼写与 allay 相近但毫无关联。

entries.definition: a Latin-rooted synonym meaning to lighten a burden.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁词源的近义词，义为「减轻负担」。

entries.definition: to remove or ease suffering; broader and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 解除或减轻痛苦；更宽泛、更日常。

entries.definition: to calm by giving in or satisfying demands.
entries.definitionCN: 以让步或满足要求来平息。

entries.definition: to soften someone's anger or anxiety.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人的怒气或焦虑软化。

normalIntro.en: Anchor allay in its root verb and its sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 把 allay 锚定在它的词根动词和音近词上。

normal.en: allay = a- + lay: literally "lay it down flat".
normal.cn: allay = a- + lay：字面就是「把它放平」。

normal.en: Fear, doubt, hunger, anger — all things you can lay to rest.
normal.cn: 恐惧、怀疑、饥饿、愤怒——都是可以「安放平息」之物。

normal.en: Not an alley (lane) and not an alloy (metal mix): one syllable stress differs.
normal.cn: 不是 alley（小巷）也不是 alloy（合金）：重音与拼写有别。

normal.en: allayed keeps the y: allay, allaying, allayed.
normal.cn: 变形保留 y：allay、allaying、allayed。

normal.en: Formal register: news headlines love "allay fears".
normal.cn: 正式语体：新闻标题爱用「allay fears（打消恐惧）」。

abstract.en: A hand gently pressing a burning spark flat until it dims.
abstract.cn: 一只手把燃烧的火星轻轻按平，直到它暗下去。

abstract.en: A worried face softens as someone lays a blanket over it.
abstract.cn: 忧虑的脸在别人盖上一条毯子后渐渐松弛。

abstract.en: Waves settling into a flat, quiet lake.
abstract.cn: 波浪平息成一片安静平整的湖面。

examples.en: The government moved quickly to allay fears of a shortage.
examples.cn: 政府迅速行动以打消对短缺的恐惧。

examples.en: A little food allayed his hunger until evening.
examples.cn: 一点食物让他的饥饿撑到了傍晚。

examples.en: Her calm voice allayed the child's anxiety.
examples.cn: 她平静的声音缓解了孩子的焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿雷」——阿婆一句“雷公别怕”，把孩子的害怕放平打雷都不怕。

root: 古英语 alecgan（a- 加强前缀 + lecgan「放平」），与 lay 同源；本义「放平、搁置」，中古英语中语义转向「平息、减轻」，与德语 legen 等日耳曼同源词一致。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from laying fear to rest, the verb reaches doubt, bodily need, anger, unrest, gradual weakening, direct reassurance, and the old physical sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 从安放恐惧出发，动词依次触及怀疑、身体需求、怒气、骚乱、渐进减弱、直接安抚，以及古老的物理义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: laying a fire low until it calms
core.cn: 核心意象：把火压低直到平静

branches.en: Fear and worry laid to rest.
branches.cn: 恐惧与忧虑被安放平息。

branches.en: Doubt and suspicion removed by reassurance.
branches.cn: 以安抚消除怀疑。

branches.en: Hunger, pain, thirst laid low.
branches.cn: 饥饿、疼痛、口渴被压下去。

branches.en: Anger and unrest cooled in people and situations.
branches.cn: 人与局势中的怒气与动荡被冷却。

branches.en: Gradual easing, direct comfort, and the archaic literal laying.
branches.cn: 渐进缓解、直接安抚，以及古旧的字面放置义。

intro.en: Allay is a compact Germanic formation, not a Latin derivative.
intro.cn: allay 是紧凑的日耳曼构词，不是拉丁派生词。

latinIntro.en: Unlike most formal verbs in this book, its root is Germanic; the Latin items below are parallel formations only.
latinIntro.cn: 与本书多数正式动词不同，它的词根是日耳曼语；下列拉丁条目仅为平行构词参考。

items.exampleCN: lay the book down（把书放下）

definition_zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言；援引作为理由
definition_en: to state that something is true or that someone did something wrong, without proof
core_image: 一个人在文件页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的事推到桌面上
scene: 调查员把一份手写材料放进档案袋，说明材料里提到的细节还没有核实。The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
sceneCN: 这里 allege 指提出尚未证实的说法（第 1 个义项：断言某事为真而尚未举证）；句意为投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。图中可辨识物件：投诉表、档案袋、手写便条、签字笔。

pos.zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言
（法律）援引、引证作为理由或依据

derivatives.zh: 指控；指称；说法
被指称的；涉嫌的
据称；据说
指称；陈述（古旧用法）

senses.title: State something as true
senses.titleCN: 指称某事为真，尚未举证
senses.definition: to state that something is the case without offering proof
senses.definitionCN: 断言某事确实如此，但未提供证据
senses.example: The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。
senses.why: Latin allegare meant 'to bring forward, adduce'; a claim is brought forward before the proof that would support it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 allegare 意为「提出、援引」；说法先被提出，支持它的证据后才可能到来。

senses.title: State it in a pleading
senses.titleCN: 在诉状或正式文书中陈述
senses.definition: to set out a fact as true in a legal or official document
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或官方文书中把某项事实陈述为真
senses.example: The plaintiff alleges that the contract was signed under duress.
senses.exampleCN: 原告主张合同是在胁迫下签署的。
senses.why: In pleadings the verb marks a fact the party undertakes to prove, so the legal sense keeps its forward-looking force.
senses.whyCN: 在诉状中，这个动词标出一项当事人承诺日后证明的事实，因此法律义保留了「向前提出」的劲头。

senses.title: Name a person's act
senses.definition: to say that a named person performed a particular act
senses.definitionCN: 指认某个具体的人做过某件具体的事
senses.example: The article alleges that two officials took payments from the contractor.
senses.exampleCN: 文章指称两名官员收受了承包商的款项。
senses.why: The pattern allege that someone did something lets a newspaper name the act while leaving the proof to others.
senses.whyCN: 「指称某人做过某事」这一结构让报纸点明行为，同时把举证留给别人。

senses.title: Cite as a reason
senses.definition: to offer something as a reason, excuse or justification
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为理由、借口或正当依据提出
senses.example: He alleged pressure from his superiors as the reason for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称上级施加的压力是延误的原因。
senses.why: Adducing a reason is literally bringing something forward, so the same verb serves for excuses and justifications.
senses.whyCN: 提供理由字面上就是把某物提出来，因此同一个动词也能用于借口与辩解。

senses.title: Cite a precedent or text
senses.definition: to quote a case, a rule or a passage in support of an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为支持论点而援引案例、规则或文句
senses.example: Counsel alleged two earlier rulings in support of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 律师援引了先前两份裁决来支持这一主张。
senses.why: A precedent is also brought forward into an argument, and the old sense of adducing survives in this usage.
senses.whyCN: 先例同样是被提出来放进论证，于是「援引」的旧义在这一用法中留存。

senses.title: Plead in excuse
senses.definition: to plead something as an excuse, an older sense now largely confined to legal and literary texts
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作辩解提出，这一旧义如今多限于法律与文学文本
senses.example: In the old account he alleged illness and left the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的记述里，他称病离开了集会。
senses.why: The older sense of adducing a defence survives in legal phrasing, where a party alleges facts to escape liability.
senses.whyCN: 「提出抗辩」的旧义残留在法律措辞里：一方援引事实以摆脱责任。

senses.title: The alleged offender
senses.titleCN: 分词形容词：被指称的，涉嫌的
senses.definition: alleged, as an adjective: named in a claim but not proved guilty
senses.definitionCN: alleged 作形容词：被指称但尚未证实有罪的
senses.example: The alleged offender was never charged.
senses.exampleCN: 被指称的涉案人从未被起诉。
senses.why: The past participle marks a person named in a claim but not yet tried, which is exactly the gap the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词标记「被指称却尚未受审」的人，正好对应这个动词所描述的缺口。

senses.title: The reported claim
senses.titleCN: 被动与副词形式：据称、据悉
senses.definition: be alleged to and allegedly: forms that report a claim while keeping the speaker at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 这类转述形式把说法归到他人名下，同时让说话者保持距离
senses.example: The firm is alleged to have moved the money offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 据称该公司把钱转移到了海外。
senses.why: Reported forms are the safest way for a paper to repeat a charge it cannot prove.
senses.whyCN: 对无法举证的指控，转述形式是报纸最稳妥的表达方式。

intro.en: Allege comes through Anglo-French aleger from Latin allegare 'to send forward, adduce', built on ad- 'to' and legare 'to send, depute'. It entered English in the fourteenth century as a pleading verb. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 来自拉丁 allegare「向前送出、援引」，由 ad-「朝向」与 legare「派出、委派」构成，十四世纪作为诉讼用语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legare meant 'to send as a deputy' and also 'to bequeath'; the root has no connection with law.
items.cn: legare 意为「作为代表派出」，也有「遗赠」义；这个词根与「法律」无关。

items.en: Ad- plus legare gave allegare 'to bring forward, adduce, plead as evidence'.
items.cn: ad- 加 legare 构成 allegare「向前提出、援引、作为证据陈说」。

items.en: Anglo-French aleger carried the legal verb into English courts in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语 aleger 在十四世纪把这个法律动词带入英格兰的法庭。

items.en: In pleading, to allege was to state a fact that the party undertook to prove later.
items.cn: 在诉讼中，allege 指陈述一项当事人承诺日后加以证明的事实。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb was used outside court for any claim put forward without proof, and the passive became the reporter's default.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词在法庭之外用于任何未经证实而提出的说法，被动式则成了报道的默认写法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the tie between legare and the root of legere 'to gather, choose' is generally thought but not proved; first records are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的词根有关，但未获证实；最早书证为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that share letters or a look with allege but not its root; group two holds verbs of asserting, ranked by how much proof they imply.
note.cn: 第一组是字母或外形与 allege 相近、却不同源的词；第二组是断言类动词，按所含证据分量排列。

entries.definition: From ligare 'to bind', so it means loyalty owed, not a claim made.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ligare「捆绑」，指所负的忠诚，而不是提出的说法。

entries.definition: From legare 'bequeath': what a will or a past age leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「遗赠」：遗嘱或过往时代留下的东西。

entries.definition: From legare 'send as a deputy': an official envoy, especially a papal one.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「作为代表派出」：官方使节，尤指教廷使节。

entries.definition: From Greek allegoria 'speaking otherwise'; a story carrying a second meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 allegoria「换个说法」：承载第二层含义的故事。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for saying something is true, with no suggestion that proof is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事为真的日常动词，不暗示缺少证据。

entries.definition: To state something confidently; it stresses the speaker's conviction rather than the lack of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地陈述某事，强调说话者的确信，而非缺少证据。

entries.definition: To say someone did wrong; it always targets a person or body, while allege often targets a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人做错事，总有一个被指对象；而 allege 常指向一件事实。

entries.definition: To argue that something is true as part of a dispute, implying opposing views.
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中主张某事为真，暗示存在对立观点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare 'send': a claim sent forward for others to test.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare「送」：把说法送到别人面前去检验。

normal.en: The family runs allege, allegation, alleged, allegedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allege、allegation、alleged 与 allegedly。

normal.en: News prose prefers the passive: the company is alleged to have...
normal.cn: 新闻语体偏爱被动式：据称该公司曾……

normal.en: A pleading alleges facts; the other side then admits or denies them.
normal.cn: 诉状提出事实主张，随后由对方承认或否认。

normal.en: Allegiance is a false friend from the binding root, not from sending.
normal.cn: allegiance 是假朋友，来自「捆绑」的词根，与「送出」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a claim pushed through a door before anyone checks who is behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个说法被推进门里，却没人先确认门后是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the foot of a page that nobody has read to the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一页没人读完的文件，页脚已经有了签名。

abstract.en: Picture a label reading reported stuck to a parcel nobody has opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着「据报」标签、却没人拆开过的包裹。

examples.en: The study alleges a link between the two chemicals and the illness.
examples.cn: 这项研究称这两种化学品与那种疾病存在关联。

examples.en: It was alleged that the files had been destroyed before the hearing.
examples.cn: 据称档案在听证之前就已被销毁。

examples.en: She alleged no reason for the delay and simply left.
examples.cn: 她没有给出延误的任何理由，就此离开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + lege（送出）」——话先送出去，证据后再补：指称、声称

root: 拉丁 allegare「向前提出、援引」= ad-（朝向）+ legare「派出、送出」；英语 allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one move: a claim is sent forward, then the settings change from court to newspaper to quotation, and finally to the grammatical forms that report it at arm's length.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：说法先被送出去，接着场景从法庭换到报纸再到引证，最后落在把那项说法隔开距离转述的语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone signs the word reported at the foot of a page and pushes the unverified sheet across the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的纸推到桌子对面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM SENT: the same move serves a newspaper sentence and a formal pleading.
branches.cn: 送出的说法：同一个动作既用于报纸句子，也用于正式诉状。

branches.en: THE ACT NAMED: a person and a deed are specified, while the proof stays elsewhere.
branches.cn: 点明的行为：指出具体的人与具体的事，证据却留在别处。

branches.en: THE REASON ADDUCED: a pressure, a precedent or a passage is brought forward in support.
branches.cn: 援引的理由：把压力、先例或文句提出来充当依据。

branches.en: THE OLD DEFENCE: pleading illness or some other fact to escape a duty belongs to an older legal idiom.
branches.cn: 古老的辩解：称病或以其他事实脱责，属于更早的法律习语。

branches.en: THE REPORTED FORM: the participle and the adverb let a writer repeat a charge without owning it.
branches.cn: 转述形式：分词与副词让写作者重复一项指控，却不必替它担保。

intro.en: Allege is a Latin verb whose prefix, root and suffixes each build other English words.
intro.cn: allege 是一个拉丁动词，前缀、词根与后缀各自还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare gives legate, legacy and legation; allege and allegation come from allegare, where ad- adds direction. Allegiance belongs to the binding root and not here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legare 衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation；allege 与 allegation 出自 allegare，由 ad- 增添方向义。allegiance 属于「捆绑」词根，不在这一族。

items.structure: ad- (Latin prefix, assimilated to al- before l)
items.example: The prefix pushes the claim into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把说法推到人前。
这个词根提供「送出」的意思。

items.meaning: to bring forward as a claim
items.example: The report alleges that the forms were altered.
items.exampleCN: 报告指称这些表格被改动过。

items.example: The alleged theft was never reported.
items.exampleCN: 被指称的盗窃从未有人报案。

items.example: The clerk allegedly deleted the file.
items.exampleCN: 据称那名职员删除了文件。

items.example: The legation closed in the spring.
items.exampleCN: 那个公使馆在春天关闭了。

items.example: The legate carried a sealed letter.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着一封密封的信。

definition_zh: 寓言；讽喻；以喻指方式表达的象征叙事
definition_en: a story, poem, or picture in which the characters and events stand for deeper moral or political meanings
core_image: 一个故事两层皮：表面是动物王国，里面全是人间
scene: 老师翻开一本写满会说话动物的书。The novel is an allegory of political power.
sceneCN: 这里的 allegory 是「寓言、讽喻」（第 1 个义项：借故事影射深层含义）；句意是这部小说是对政治权力的讽喻。

derivatives.zh: 由 allegory 加 -ical 构成，义为「寓言的；讽喻的」
由 allegorical 加 -ly 构成，义为「以讽喻方式」
由 allegory 加 -ize 构成，义为「把……寓言化」
由 allegory 加 -ist 构成，义为「寓言作家」

senses.title: A narrative with a hidden second meaning
senses.definition: a story in which characters and events symbolize deeper moral or political meanings
senses.definitionCN: 人物与事件象征更深的道德或政治含义的故事
senses.example: Animal Farm is an allegory of the Russian Revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 《动物农场》是对俄国革命的讽喻。
senses.why: The Greek root means "speaking otherwise", so the core image is a story saying one thing and meaning another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根本义是「换个说法」，核心意象即故事表面说一事、内里指另一事。

senses.title: The allegorical method of interpretation
senses.definition: the practice of interpreting a text as carrying hidden symbolic meanings
senses.definitionCN: 把文本解读为暗含象征意义的做法
senses.example: Early scholars treated the epic through allegory.
senses.exampleCN: 早期学者以寓意法解读这部史诗。
senses.why: From naming the work, the word extends to naming the way of reading it.
senses.whyCN: 由指称作品扩展到指称解读方式。

senses.title: A symbolic representation in art
senses.definition: a painting, sculpture, or other work in which figures symbolize abstract ideas
senses.definitionCN: 以形象象征抽象思想的绘画、雕塑等作品
senses.example: The mural is an allegory of justice.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画是正义的象征性表现。
senses.why: Visual art borrows the same double-layer structure from narrative.
senses.whyCN: 视觉艺术借用了叙事同样的双层结构。

senses.title: An emblem or visible symbol of an idea
senses.definition: a figure or emblem regarded as the embodiment of an abstract concept
senses.definitionCN: 被视为抽象概念化身的形象或标志
senses.example: The blindfolded figure became an allegory of fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 蒙眼的形象成了公平的化身。
senses.why: A single image can carry the whole hidden meaning, like a one-figure allegory.
senses.whyCN: 单个形象可以承载全部隐义，如同单人物的寓言。

senses.title: Political satire in story form
senses.titleCN: 以故事形式的政治讽刺
senses.definition: a narrative that criticizes political power through symbolic displacement
senses.definitionCN: 通过象征性移置来批评政治权力的叙事
senses.example: The play works as an allegory of dictatorship.
senses.exampleCN: 这出戏起到了讽喻独裁的作用。
senses.why: Symbolic distance lets writers attack power safely, a natural extension of the double layer.
senses.whyCN: 象征的距离让作者能安全地抨击权力，这是双层结构的自然延伸。

senses.title: Religious and moral instruction through story
senses.titleCN: 借故事进行的宗教道德教化
senses.definition: a didactic story used to teach religious or moral lessons
senses.definitionCN: 用于传授宗教或道德教训的说教故事
senses.example: The old tale is a moral allegory of temptation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老故事是关于诱惑的道德寓言。
senses.why: Teaching through symbols is the oldest use of speaking otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 借象征施教是「换个说法」最古老的用途。

senses.title: A sustained metaphor governing a whole work
senses.definition: an extended metaphor whose logic organizes an entire text or work
senses.definitionCN: 其逻辑组织起整个文本的延展隐喻
senses.example: The voyage becomes an extended allegory of a life.
senses.exampleCN: 航程成为人生的整体隐喻。
senses.why: When one metaphor runs a whole story, the two layers lock together.
senses.whyCN: 当一个隐喻贯穿整个故事时，两层含义便锁定在一起。

senses.title: The genre or tradition of such works
senses.definition: allegorical writing considered as a literary genre or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 作为文学文类或传统的寓言写作
senses.example: Medieval allegory flourished for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪寓言兴盛数百年。
senses.why: A practice shared by many works becomes a nameable tradition.
senses.whyCN: 许多作品共有的写作方式汇成可命名的传统。

intro.en: Allegory comes from Greek allegoria, "speaking otherwise", via Latin into the European languages.
intro.cn: allegory 源自希腊语 allegoria「换个说法」，经拉丁语进入欧洲诸语言。

items.en: Root *gerbh-, "to scratch, carve" (speech as carving), reconstructed.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gerbh-「刻画」（言语如刻画）。

items.en: allos "other" + agoreuein "speak in the assembly"; allegoria "speaking otherwise".
items.cn: 希腊语 allos「另一个」+ agoreuein「在集会上讲」，allegoria 即「换个说法」。

items.en: allegoria borrowed as a rhetorical term by Cicero and Quintilian.
items.cn: 拉丁语 allegoria 作为修辞学术语被西塞罗、昆体良借用。

items.en: allegorie, the channel into English.
items.cn: 古法语 allegorie，进入英语的通道。

items.en: allegorie/allegory appears in Middle English literary criticism.
items.cn: allegory 出现于中古英语文学批评。

items.en: Standard term for symbolic narrative and its interpretation.
items.cn: 如今是象征叙事及其解读的标准术语。

note.en: Allegory overlaps with fable, parable, and metaphor, and differs from the look-alike alley in spelling only.
note.cn: allegory 与 fable、parable、metaphor 意义相近，与 alley 仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: to claim without proof; shares the Greek allos element but a different verb root.
entries.definitionCN: 指控、声称；共享希腊语 allos 成分但动词词根不同。

entries.definition: a narrow lane; similar letters only, unrelated origin.
entries.definitionCN: 小巷；仅字母相似，词源无关。

entries.definition: a medical hypersensitivity; both come from Greek allos "other", but the meanings diverged completely.
entries.definitionCN: 过敏；同出希腊语 allos「另一个」，但语义已完全分化。

entries.definition: a short tale with animal characters and an explicit moral.
entries.definitionCN: 篇幅短小、动物主角、明言教训的故事。

entries.definition: a simple story teaching a religious or ethical lesson.
entries.definitionCN: 传授宗教或伦理教训的简明故事。

entries.definition: a figure of speech; allegory is in effect a sustained metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 修辞格；寓言实质上是延展的隐喻。

normalIntro.en: Build allegory from its Greek parts.
normalIntro.cn: 用希腊语构件搭建 allegory。

normal.en: allos "other" + agoreuein "speak": speaking otherwise.
normal.cn: allos「另一个」+ agoreuein「说」：换个说法。

normal.en: Compare allergy: same allos "other", a body reacting to the "other".
normal.cn: 对比 allergy：同一个 allos「另一个」，身体对「异物」起反应。

normal.en: Compare allege: claiming "otherwise" than what is proven.
normal.cn: 对比 allege：声称与已证事实「不同」的说法。

normal.en: Animal Farm, Pilgrim's Progress, Plato's cave: the classic trio.
normal.cn: 《动物农场》《天路历程》、柏拉图洞穴：经典三部曲。

normal.en: adjective allegorical, verb allegorize, person allegorist.
normal.cn: 形容词 allegorical、动词 allegorize、人物 allegorist。

abstract.en: A stage curtain: in front, a children's tale; behind it, a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 一道舞台幕布：前面是童话，后面是法庭。

abstract.en: A wolf in a suit giving a speech to sheep.
abstract.cn: 一只穿西装的狼向羊群演讲。

abstract.en: Two layers of glass with different paintings, seen at once.
abstract.cn: 两层玻璃各绘一画，叠看之下同时显现。

examples.en: Critics read the film as an allegory of immigration.
examples.cn: 评论家把这部电影解读为关于移民的讽喻。

examples.en: The painter filled the canvas with allegories of the seasons.
examples.cn: 画家在画布上画满了四季的寓意形象。

examples.en: Medieval writers composed long religious allegories.
examples.cn: 中世纪作家创作了长篇宗教寓言。

sensesIntro.en: From the double-layered story itself, the senses spread to the method of reading, visual art, emblems, political satire, moral teaching, extended metaphor, and the genre as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 从双层故事本身出发，义项扩展到解读方法、视觉艺术、寓意形象、政治讽刺、道德教化、延展隐喻以及作为整体的文类。

core.cn: 核心意象：表面说一事、内里指另一事的故事

branches.en: The narrative with symbolic second meaning.
branches.cn: 具有象征第二义的叙事。

branches.en: Reading texts as symbolic.
branches.cn: 把文本当象征来读的方法。

branches.en: The same structure in visual art and emblems.
branches.cn: 同一结构在视觉艺术与寓意形象中。

branches.cn: 对权力的讽刺与道德教化。

branches.cn: 延展隐喻与文类传统。

intro.cn: allegory 可分解为希腊语「另一个」加一个公开言说的动词。

latinIntro.en: The word passed through Latin rhetoric almost unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经拉丁语修辞学传入，几乎未变。

latinEntries.example: Cicero uses allegoria in rhetorical works
latinEntries.exampleCN: 西塞罗在修辞著作中使用 allegoria

definition_zh: 小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道；死胡同
definition_en: a narrow passage between buildings, a bowling lane, or a garden path
core_image: 两堵高墙夹出的一条窄缝，尽头才见一点光
scene: 孩子把球滚进两栋楼之间的窄巷，转身就跑。The cat dashed into a narrow alley between the two buildings.
sceneCN: 这里 alley 是「小巷」（第 1 个义项：建筑之间的狭窄通道）；句意为猫冲进两栋楼之间的窄巷。

pos.zh: 名词：小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道

derivatives.zh: 由 alley 与 way 构成的复合名词，义为「小巷；窄道」
复合名词，义为「流浪猫」，指在巷子里讨生活的猫
复合名词，义为「保龄球馆」或「保龄球道」
复合名词，义为「死胡同」，也比喻没有前途的办法

senses.title: A narrow passage between buildings
senses.definition: a narrow street or passage running between or behind buildings
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之间或后方延伸的狭窄街道或通道
senses.example: They met in an alley behind the market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在市场后面的一条小巷里见面。
senses.why: Old French alee meant a walking or a passage, from the verb to go; an alley is a route squeezed between walls.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 alee 意为行走或通道，来自表示「走」的动词；alley 就是被墙夹出来的一条路线。

senses.title: A bowling lane
senses.definition: the long narrow track down which a bowling ball is rolled
senses.definitionCN: 供保龄球滚向球瓶的长而窄的球道
senses.example: The ball curved across the alley and hit the last pin.
senses.exampleCN: 球斜穿过球道，击中了最后一只瓶。
senses.why: A bowling lane has exactly the shape of an alley: a long narrow strip with walls or gutters on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 保龄球道的形状正像一条小巷：长而窄，两侧有边沟或挡板。

senses.title: A garden path
senses.definition: a narrow path in a garden or park, often bordered by plants
senses.definitionCN: 花园或公园中的狭窄小径，常由植物镶边
senses.example: A gravel alley led from the gate to the roses.
senses.exampleCN: 一条碎石小径从门口通向玫瑰丛。
senses.why: The passage does not need buildings: any narrow way meant for walking can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 通道不一定需要建筑：任何供人行走的窄路都能用这个名字。

senses.title: A blind alley: no way forward
senses.definition: a course of action that leads nowhere, from the image of a passage with no exit
senses.definitionCN: 指走不通的做法，来自没有出口的通道这一意象
senses.example: Endless testing was a blind alley for the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 无止境的测试对研究团队来说是条死胡同。
senses.why: A real alley can end at a wall; the mind borrows that wall for any plan that cannot continue.
senses.whyCN: 真实的小巷可以在墙前终止；头脑把那堵墙借给任何无法继续的计划。

intro.en: Alley comes from a French verb meaning to go, and its narrow shape then spread to bowling and to dead ends.
intro.cn: alley 来自一个意为「走」的法语动词，它狭窄的形状随后延伸到保龄球与死胡同。

items.en: Latin ambulare meant to walk about, and it is the distant source of alley and of amble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare 意为到处走动，是 alley 与 amble 的远源。

items.en: Old French aler meant to go, and its participle alee named a going or a passage.
items.cn: 古法语 aler 意为去、走，其分词形式 alee 指一次行走或一条通道。

items.en: Middle English took the word as aley, a narrow way for walking.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入作 aley，指供行走的窄路。

items.en: The long narrow lane of a bowling game borrowed the shape and the name.
items.cn: 保龄球那长而窄的球道借用了这个形状，也借用了这个名字。

items.en: Garden paths used the word for any narrow walk bordered by plants.
items.cn: 花园小径用这个词指任何由植物镶边的窄走道。

items.en: The phrase blind alley extended the physical dead end into a failed plan.
items.cn: 短语 blind alley 把物理上的死胡同延伸到失败的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers alley compounds; the near-meaning group gathers narrow ways and passages.
note.cn: 形近组收 alley 的复合词；近义组收狭窄的道路与通道。

entries.definition: A narrow passage, often between buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭窄通道，常在建筑之间。

entries.definition: A stray cat that lives in streets and alleys.
entries.definitionCN: 指在街巷里生活的流浪猫。

entries.definition: A building or lane for bowling.
entries.definitionCN: 指打保龄球的场馆或球道。

entries.definition: A passage with no exit, or a plan that cannot succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有出口的通道，或无法成功的计划。

entries.definition: A narrow road in the country or a marked strip of a wider road.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡间窄路，或宽路上划出的一条车道。

entries.definition: A way through or along which someone or something passes.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或物穿行而过的通道。

entries.definition: A track made by walking, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 指走出来的小路，多在户外。

entries.definition: A long passage inside a building or between rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑内部或房间之间的长通道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the narrow gap and then stretch it into a bowling lane and a dead end.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子先抓住那条窄缝，再把它拉成保龄球道与死胡同。

normal.en: Alley is a walking passage squeezed between two walls, so narrowness is the core.
normal.cn: alley 是被两堵墙夹出来的行走通道，所以「窄」是核心。

normal.en: A bowling alley is an alley laid flat and given pins.
normal.cn: bowling alley 是把小巷放平，再摆上球瓶。

normal.en: A garden alley is the same narrow walk with flowers instead of walls.
normal.cn: 花园小径是同一种窄走道，只是把墙换成了花。

normal.en: A blind alley ends at a wall, so the phrase means a plan that cannot go on.
normal.cn: blind alley 终止于一堵墙，所以这个短语指无法继续的计划。

normal.en: An alley cat lives in the gaps between buildings, not in a house.
normal.cn: alley cat 住在建筑之间的缝隙里，而不是住在屋里。

abstract.en: Picture two high brick walls almost touching, with a thin strip of sky above them.
abstract.cn: 想象两堵高高的砖墙几乎相碰，上方只留一条细细的天空。

abstract.en: Lay the strip down horizontally and it becomes a lane with a ball rolling along it.
abstract.cn: 把这条缝横过来放平，它就成了一条有球滚过的球道。

abstract.en: Put a wall across the far end and the same strip becomes a blind alley.
abstract.cn: 在远端横上一堵墙，同一条缝就成了死胡同。

examples.en: The delivery van blocked the narrow alley behind the shop.
examples.cn: 送货的面包车堵住了商店后面的窄巷。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon at a bowling alley near the station.
examples.cn: 他们一下午都待在车站附近的保龄球馆。

examples.en: The committee realized the old plan was a blind alley.
examples.cn: 委员会意识到旧方案是一条死胡同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱理」——爱理不理，只肯走那条没人理的小巷

root: 经由古法语 alee（行走、通道）来自拉丁语 ambulare（走动）；本指两墙之间的窄路，后引申指保龄球道、花园小径，并以 blind alley 比喻无出路的办法。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all keep the shape of a long narrow strip, filled with walls, gutters, plants, or a final barrier.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「长而窄的一条」这个形状，只是填进去的是墙、边沟、植物或一道终点屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls stand almost touching, and a thin line of light runs between them toward the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙几乎相贴，一线光在它们之间一直延伸到远端。

branches.en: THE GAP: the first sense is a way for people squeezed between buildings.
branches.cn: 缝隙线：第一个义项是人们在建筑之间挤过去的路。

branches.en: THE LANE: the same strip lies flat and becomes a track for a rolling ball.
branches.cn: 球道线：同一条窄带放平，就成了滚球的轨道。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: walls give way to plants, but the narrow walk remains.
branches.cn: 花园线：墙换成了植物，窄走道仍然保留。

branches.en: THE WALL: when the far end is closed, the passage becomes a metaphor for failure.
branches.cn: 墙线：远端被封住时，通道就成了失败的比喻。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN WAY: an alley is often a route people use to avoid the main street.
branches.cn: 暗线：小巷常是人们避开主街时走的路线。

intro.en: Alley is a French loanword with a small family built by compounding rather than suffixation.
intro.cn: alley 是法语借词，小词族靠复合构词而不是后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin ambulare, but it entered English through French, so the Latin entries are indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词上溯至拉丁语 ambulare，但经法语进入英语，因此拉丁条目是间接的。

items.example: The alley was too narrow for a car.
items.exampleCN: 这条小巷窄得车开不进去。

items.example: It is the distant source of alley.

items.exampleCN: 它的分词形式产生了 alee。

items.example: They walked through a dark alleyway.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一条黑暗的窄道。

items.example: An alley cat slept on the bins.
items.exampleCN: 一只流浪猫睡在垃圾桶上。

items.meaning: a place or lane for bowling
items.example: The bowling alley was full on Friday.
The route ended in a blind alley.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线终止在一条死胡同里。

definition_zh: 联盟；同盟；结盟关系；（旧）姻亲关系
definition_en: a union of countries or groups formed for a shared purpose, or the relationship created by such a union
core_image: 两户人家把各自的门闩用一根粗绳系在一起
scene: 两个小国面对同一个强敌，签下条约把军队交给同一名指挥官。The two countries formed an alliance against the invaders.
sceneCN: 这里的 alliance 是「联盟」（第 1 个义项：国家为共同目的结成的同盟）；句意是两国结成联盟抵御入侵者。

pos.zh: 名词：联盟；同盟；结盟关系；姻亲关系

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「盟友」，也可作动词「结盟」
由 ally 加 -ed 构成，义为「结盟的；同盟的」
同源词，义为「效忠；忠诚」，与拉丁语「捆绑」词根相关
由 mis- 加 alliance 构成，义为「不般配的结合」

senses.title: A union of states for a common aim
senses.definition: a formal union of two or more states or governments that agree to act together, especially in war or defence
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个国家或政府为共同行动、尤其在战争或防务上合作而结成的正式联合
senses.example: The two kingdoms sealed an alliance that lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 两个王国缔结了一项持续四十年的同盟。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning 'to bind'; an alliance is literally a binding of separate parties, and states bind themselves by treaty so that each must move with the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「捆绑」的动词；alliance 字面上就是把彼此分开的各方绑在一起，国家通过条约把自己绑住，因此一方行动时另一方也受到牵制。

senses.title: A coalition of groups or people
senses.titleCN: 团体或个人的联合；同盟
senses.definition: a union of organisations, parties, or individuals who cooperate for a shared purpose without merging into one body
senses.definitionCN: 组织、政党或个人为共同目标合作而形成的联合，但并不合并为一个整体
senses.example: An alliance of small shops negotiated a lower rent together.
senses.exampleCN: 一些小店铺组成联盟，一起谈下了更低的租金。
senses.why: The binding image transfers easily from states to any parties: what matters is the pledge to act together, not the size of the members, so the word covers shopkeepers and parties as well as nations.
senses.whyCN: 「捆绑」的意象很容易从国家转到任何团体：关键在共同行动的承诺，而不在成员大小，所以小店主、政党乃至个人都能用 alliance 来形容这种联合。

senses.title: Kinship by marriage
senses.definition: a relationship created by marriage between families, an older sense still found in historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 家族之间因婚姻而形成的关系，这是较旧的义项，仍见于历史文献
senses.example: The noble houses sought an alliance through the marriage of their eldest children.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个贵族家族想通过长子女的婚姻建立姻亲关系。
senses.why: Marriage also binds two families, so the same word once served for a political treaty and for a wedding; modern usage keeps the political sense and leaves this one to histories and genealogies.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻同样把两个家族绑在一起，所以这个词过去既指政治盟约也指婚事；现代用法保留了政治义，把姻亲义留给历史与族谱类文本。

intro.en: Alliance is a binding word: it goes back to a Latin verb for tying things together.
intro.cn: alliance 是一个「捆绑」的词：源头是拉丁语中表示把东西系在一起的动词。

items.en: ligare meant 'to tie, bind', and it also produced ligature and obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为「系、捆、绑」，它还生出 ligature 与 obligation 等词。

items.en: The prefixed verb alligare meant 'to bind to something', with ad- adding the idea of direction towards.
items.cn: 加前缀的动词 alligare 意为「绑到某物上」，ad- 补出「朝向」的方向感。

items.en: Old French alier and its noun form developed the political sense of joining parties by agreement.
items.cn: 古法语 alier 及其名词形式发展出「以协议把各方联合起来」的政治义。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century, first for marriage ties and treaties, then for any league of parties.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个名词，最初指婚姻联系与条约，后来泛指任何团体的联合。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from military alliances to alliances of companies, while the marriage sense survives mainly in historical writing.
items.cn: 现代用法从军事同盟延伸到企业联盟，姻亲义则主要留在历史叙述里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for binding; the near-meaning group gathers leagues and pacts of different strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「捆绑」词根；近义组收不同紧密程度的同盟与协定。

entries.definition: a person or state that has agreed to help another
entries.definitionCN: 盟友；同盟国

entries.definition: joined by agreement; related
entries.definitionCN: 结盟的；有关联的

entries.definition: loyalty owed to a ruler, state, or cause
entries.definitionCN: 效忠；忠诚

entries.definition: an unsuitable marriage or partnership
entries.definitionCN: 不般配的婚姻或结合

entries.definition: a temporary union of parties that keep their own identity
entries.definitionCN: 各党保持自身身份的临时联合

entries.definition: a group of states or teams joined for a common purpose
entries.definitionCN: 同盟；联赛

entries.definition: a formal agreement between two parties
entries.definitionCN: 协定；条约

entries.definition: a loose union of states that keep most powers
entries.definitionCN: 邦联；松散的联合

normalIntro.en: Alliance is the noun of binding: parties tied by a promise to act together.
normalIntro.cn: alliance 是「捆绑」的名词：各方被一个共同行动的承诺系在一起。

normal.en: Remember lig-: the same root as ligament, a band that ties.
normal.cn: 记住词根 lig-：与 ligament（韧带）同源，都是把东西系住。

normal.en: Form an alliance is the usual verb phrase.
normal.cn: form an alliance 是最常见的动词搭配。

normal.en: The preposition is with: in alliance with.
normal.cn: 介词用 with：in alliance with。

normal.en: An alliance can be broken, dissolved, or forged.
normal.cn: 联盟可以被 break、dissolve 或 forge。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with allegiance, which is loyalty.
normal.cn: 不要与 allegiance（效忠）混淆。

abstract.en: Picture two door bars tied by one rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两根门闩被一根绳子系在一起。

abstract.en: See two hands clasped over a signed paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在签好的文件上方握在一起。

abstract.en: Imagine two armies marching under one flag.
abstract.cn: 想象两支军队在同一面旗下行进。

examples.en: The two countries formed an alliance to protect their shared border.
examples.cn: 两国结成联盟，共同守卫边界。

examples.en: Several local charities work in alliance with the city council.
examples.cn: 几家本地慈善机构与市议会合作。

examples.en: The alliance between the two parties collapsed after the budget vote.
examples.cn: 预算表决之后，两党之间的联盟瓦解了。

dict_mnemonic.text: al-（向）+ li（绑，同 lig-）+ -ance（名词）——绑在一起，就是同盟。

root: 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」加 ad- 构成 alligare「绑到某物上」，经古法语 alier 及其名词形式进入英语；十四世纪借入时兼指婚姻联系与政治条约，后来泛指各类团体的联合。

sensesIntro.en: One binding image yields three uses: states tied by treaty, groups tied by a shared aim, and families once tied by marriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「捆绑」意象生出三种用法：以条约相连的国家、以共同目标相连的团体，以及旧时以婚姻相连的家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two door bars joined by one rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根门闩被一根绳子系在一起。

branches.en: two kingdoms signing a treaty of defence
branches.cn: 两个王国签订防御条约

branches.en: an alliance that lasted forty years
branches.cn: 持续四十年的同盟

branches.en: small shops bargaining together
branches.cn: 小店铺联合起来谈判

intro.en: A Latin root for binding, with relatives that range from ligaments to loyalty.
intro.cn: 一个表示「捆绑」的拉丁词根，其同源词从韧带一直延伸到忠诚。

latinIntro.en: Ligare is the Latin verb at the centre of this family.
latinIntro.cn: ligare 是这个词族的中心动词。

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派（任务）；把（成本）分摊到科目
definition_en: to give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose, or to assign a duty or cost to someone
core_image: 一张长桌上摆着几只空盘子，厨师按人数把菜一份份分进去
scene: 市政会议开到深夜，争论的焦点是钱该往哪里花。The council allocated half the budget to road repairs.
sceneCN: 这里的 allocate 是「分配、拨给」（第 1 个义项：把钱或资源按用途分出）；句意是市议会把一半预算拨给了道路维修。

pos.zh: 动词：分配；拨给；分派；分摊

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「分配；拨款；配额」
由 re- 加 allocate 构成，义为「重新分配」
由 allocation 加 -ive 构成，义为「与分配有关的」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「分配者；分配程序」

senses.title: To give out money or resources
senses.definition: to set apart and give out money, materials, or other resources for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途划出并发放资金、物资或其他资源
senses.example: The hospital allocated two million pounds to new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 医院拨出两百万英镑购置新设备。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and ad- added 'to'; to allocate is to place something into a particular slot, so money is put where the purpose requires it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为「放置」，ad- 表示「到」；allocate 就是「放到某个位置上」，钱被放进为它指定的那一格，所以既可译「分配」也可译「拨给」。

senses.title: To assign a duty or role
senses.definition: to give a particular job, duty, or role to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作、职责或角色交给某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The teacher allocated each group a different part of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把项目的不同部分分派给各个小组。
senses.why: The same 'placing' works for tasks: a duty is put into someone's hands, and the person becomes the slot it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「放置」也适用于任务：职责被放进某人手里，那个人就成了这项职责所在的位置，因此 allocate 常与 tasks、duties、roles 搭配。

senses.title: To apportion costs in accounting
senses.definition: to divide a cost or revenue among accounts, departments, or periods in bookkeeping
senses.definitionCN: 在记账中把成本或收入分摊到各科目、各部门或各期间
senses.example: The firm allocated the overhead costs across its three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把间接费用分摊到三个分部。
senses.why: In accounting the 'placing' becomes a division: one total is cut into shares and each share is placed on the account that caused it, which is why the verb appears with costs and overhead.
senses.whyCN: 在会计里，「放置」变成了「切分」：一笔总额被切成若干份，每一份放进造成它的那个科目，所以这个义项的宾语常见 costs、overhead 这类词。

intro.en: Allocate is a bookkeeping word at heart: it comes from a Latin verb for placing something in a spot.
intro.cn: allocate 骨子里是个记账词：它来自拉丁语中表示「把东西放到某处」的动词。

items.en: locus meant 'place, spot', and it also gave English local and locate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，英语的 local 与 locate 也由它而来。

items.en: locare meant 'to place, set, arrange', and was used of putting things or persons in position.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安置、安排」，用于把物品或人放到位置上。

items.en: The prefixed form allocare is recorded in medieval Latin with the sense 'to place to, assign', especially in accounts.
items.cn: 加前缀的形式 allocare 见于中世纪拉丁语，义为「放置到、分派」，尤用于账目。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; early examples already concern money and shares.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，早期用例已经与钱款和份额有关。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb from budgets to tasks, seats, time slots, and computing memory.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从预算扩展到任务、座位、时间段以及计算机内存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb for placing; the near-meaning group gathers ways of giving out shares with different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「放置」动词；近义组收发放份额的各种说法，侧重各有不同。

items.meaning: the act of assigning; a share

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派（时间、金钱、土地等）
definition_en: to give a share of time, money, land, or work to someone or for a purpose
core_image: 把一块饼按人头切开分下去
scene: 主持人举起手表宣布规则。Each speaker is allotted five minutes.
sceneCN: 这里的 allot 是「分配、拨给」（第 1 个义项：按份额分派）；句意是每位发言者被分配五分钟。

derivatives.zh: 由 allot 加 -ment 构成，义为「分配；份额；拨地」
拉丁同族词，义为「配给；拨款」
拉丁同族动词，义为「分配；配置」

senses.title: To assign a share of something
senses.definition: to give someone a fixed share of time, money, or resources
senses.definitionCN: 把固定份额的时间、金钱或资源分给某人
senses.example: The committee allotted each project a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会给每个项目分配了预算。
senses.why: From "assign by lot": shares are fixed as surely as drawn lots.
senses.whyCN: 源于「按签分配」：份额像抽签一样被固定下来。

senses.title: To set aside for a purpose
senses.definition: to reserve an amount of something for a specific use
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途预留一定数量
senses.example: Two hours were allotted for questions.
senses.exampleCN: 问答环节被安排了两个小时。
senses.why: Assigning to a person widens to assigning to a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 分派给人扩展为分派给用途。

senses.title: To distribute land officially
senses.definition: to divide and grant land, especially by formal decision
senses.definitionCN: 划分并授予土地，尤指经正式决定
senses.example: The government allotted plots to settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 政府把地块分给移民。
senses.why: Historically tied to land distribution by drawn lots.
senses.whyCN: 历史上与抽签分地紧密相关。

senses.title: To apportion duties or tasks
senses.definition: to divide work among people according to a plan
senses.definitionCN: 按计划把工作分给众人
senses.example: The captain allotted duties to the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把任务分派给船员。
senses.why: The share logic applies to labor as well as property.
senses.whyCN: 份额的逻辑同样适用于劳力。

senses.title: To grant as one's due portion
senses.definition: to give someone what is judged their proper share
senses.definitionCN: 把被认定应得的份额给予某人
senses.example: Each heir was allotted a fair portion.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人都分得公平的一份。
senses.why: Drawing lots was a way of deciding what was fairly due.
senses.whyCN: 抽签本是决定公平应得的方式。

senses.title: To fix or appoint in advance
senses.definition: to fix or assign something, such as a slot, in advance
senses.definitionCN: 预先固定或指定某物，如时段
senses.example: A fixed slot is allotted to each candidate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位候选人被指定固定时段。
senses.why: Once the lot is drawn, the assignment is settled beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 签一抽定，指派便预先落定。

senses.title: Allot (archaic): to assign by lot
senses.definition: in the original and archaic sense, to distribute by drawing lots
senses.definitionCN: 最初与古旧义项：以抽签方式分发
senses.example: The land was allotted by lot in old custom.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧俗，土地以抽签方式分配。
senses.why: This is the literal source sense preserved in the etymology.
senses.whyCN: 这是保留在词源中的字面本义。

senses.title: Allot (passive): to be given as one's lot
senses.titleCN: 被动义：被派得（命运所定的一份）
senses.definition: in passive use, to fall to someone as if assigned by fate
senses.definitionCN: 被动用法中指如同命中注定般落到某人身上
senses.example: Such burdens were allotted to the eldest.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的重担落在了长子身上。
senses.why: Lots were fate; whatever the lot assigned became one's destiny.
senses.whyCN: 签即命运；抽到什么，什么便成为注定的一份。

intro.en: Allot is a native formation: the French-style prefix a- plus lot, "that which is drawn".
intro.cn: allot 是本土构词：法语式前缀 a- 加 lot「被抽中的签」。

items.en: Reconstructed *hluta-, "share obtained by lot".
items.cn: 重构词形 *hluta-「抽签所得的份」。

items.en: hlot, the object drawn to decide a share; source of lot.
items.cn: 古英语 hlot，用于抽签定份额的物件，即 lot 的来源。

items.en: a + lot → alotten, "to assign by lot".
items.cn: 中古英语 a + lot → alotten「按签指派」。

items.en: allot attested with the modern spelling and sense.
items.cn: 十五世纪 allot 以现代拼写与词义见于文献。

items.en: Widespread in legal and administrative English.
items.cn: 广泛用于法律与行政英语。

items.en: Formal verb for assigning shares; noun allotment common in British English.
items.cn: 正式动词，指分配份额；英式英语中名词 allotment 常用。

note.en: Allot is easily confused with the similar-sounding aloud, and is close in meaning to allocate and assign.
note.cn: allot 易与发音相近的 aloud 混淆，意义上与 allocate、assign 接近。

entries.definition: out loud; different final consonant and unrelated meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 出声地；词尾辅音不同，意义无关。

entries.definition: the noun for a share or grant allotted.
entries.definitionCN: 分配所得的份额或拨地。

entries.definition: a voting slip; historically also "little ball" used to draw lots, a parallel to lot but from Italian.
entries.definitionCN: 选票；历史上亦指用于抽签的小球，与 lot 平行但源自意大利语，并非同根。

entries.definition: the Latin-rooted near synonym, common in economics and computing.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁词源的近义词，常见于经济与计算机领域。

entries.definition: to give out tasks or marks; broader than allot.
entries.definitionCN: 分派任务或分数；比 allot 更宽泛。

entries.definition: to divide into proportional shares.
entries.definitionCN: 按比例划分份额。

normalIntro.cn: 把 allot 与 lot 及其双写字母绑在一起记。

normal.cn: allot = a- + lot：按签分配。

normal.en: Double the t: allotted, allotting — like bigotted style doubling.
normal.cn: 双写 t：allotted、allotting。

normal.en: Time, money, land, duty: the four classic objects of allot.
normal.cn: 时间、金钱、土地、职责：allot 的四大经典宾语。

normal.en: Noun allotment; cousin verbs allocate, assign, apportion.
normal.cn: 名词 allotment；同义动词 allocate、assign、apportion。

normal.en: Not aloud: allot ends in the /t/ sound.
normal.cn: 不是 aloud：allot 以 /t/ 音结尾。

abstract.en: Straws of different length drawn from a closed fist.
abstract.cn: 从紧握的拳中抽出长短不一的草签。

abstract.en: A pie cut into equal wedges, one per person.
abstract.cn: 一块饼被切成均等的楔形，一人一块。

abstract.en: A clock face with one sector shaded: your allotted time.
abstract.cn: 钟面被划出一格阴影：那是分给你的时间。

examples.en: Only thirty minutes were allotted for the test.
examples.cn: 考试只分配了三十分钟。

examples.en: The city allotted funds for new parks.
examples.cn: 市政府为新建公园拨了款。

examples.en: Tasks were allotted according to experience.
examples.cn: 任务按经验分派。

root: 古英语 hlot「抽签用的签、阄」（日耳曼语源，与德语 Los 同源）→ 中古英语 a-（加强前缀，仿法语动词构词）+ lot 构成 alotten「按签分配」→ 现代英语 allot；名词 lot「签、份」同根。

sensesIntro.en: Beginning with assigning shares, the verb moves to reserving for purposes, granting land, apportioning work and dues, fixing in advance, and finally the literal drawing of lots and fateful assignment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分配份额出发，动词依次覆盖预留用途、授予土地、分派工作与应得份、预先固定，最后回到抽签本义与命运派定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shares fixed as if drawn by lot
core.cn: 核心意象：如抽签般被固定的份额

branches.en: Shares and purposes to which amounts are fixed.
branches.cn: 份额与被指定用途。

branches.en: Land grants and work divided among people.
branches.cn: 土地授予与工作分派。

branches.en: Each one's fair due.
branches.cn: 各自应得的公平一份。

branches.en: Slots fixed in advance.
branches.cn: 预先固定的时段。

branches.en: The literal lot-drawing and fate-like assignment.
branches.cn: 字面抽签与命运般的派定。

intro.cn: allot 把日耳曼名词与法语式前缀结合。

latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼一支为本族词；拉丁条目仅为平行近义词。

definition_zh: 分配；份额；拨给的土地；（英）小块租种地
definition_en: an amount allotted to a person or purpose, or a small plot of land rented for growing vegetables
core_image: 写着你名字的一小块地/一份额
scene: 城边空地上排着一格格的小菜园。Grandfather grows beans on his allotment.
sceneCN: 这里的 allotment 是「小块租种地」（第 3 个义项：英国城郊分给居民种菜的地块）；句意是爷爷在他的租种地上种豆子。

senses.title: The act of allotting
senses.definition: the act or process of allotting shares, funds, or tasks
senses.definitionCN: 分配份额、资金或任务的行为或过程
senses.example: The allotment of duties took all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 分派任务花了整个上午。
senses.why: The -ment suffix turns the verb allot into the action or its result.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词 allot 转为动作或其结果。

senses.title: The share or amount allotted
senses.definition: the amount or quota allotted to a person, unit, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 分给个人、单位或用途的数量或配额
senses.example: His allotment of grain was cut in half.
senses.exampleCN: 他的粮食配给被削减了一半。
senses.why: From the act to its concrete result: what you receive.
senses.whyCN: 由动作转到具体结果：你实际得到的份。

senses.title: A British vegetable plot for rent
senses.definition: in Britain, a small plot of land rented from a council for growing vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 英国指从市政租来种菜的小块土地
senses.example: There is a waiting list for allotments in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的租种地要排队等候。
senses.why: Land was literally allotted to townspeople; the grant hardened into the place name.
senses.whyCN: 土地确曾分配给市民；这种授予固化成了地名性的用法。

senses.title: A grant of land to a person or group
senses.definition: an official grant of land, especially historically to Native Americans or settlers
senses.definitionCN: 官方拨予的土地，尤指历史上给原住民或移民的份地
senses.example: Each family received a land allotment.
senses.exampleCN: 每户家庭获得一份拨地。
senses.why: The legal act of allotting land left a noun for the granted parcel itself.
senses.whyCN: 拨地这一法律行为留下了指称所拨地块本身的名词。

senses.title: A share of stock in issue
senses.definition: shares of a new issue assigned to an applicant
senses.definitionCN: 新股发行中分派给申购者的股份
senses.example: Her application got a small allotment of shares.
senses.exampleCN: 她的申购获得了少量股份配售。
senses.why: Finance keeps the drawing-of-lots flavor in distributing new issues.
senses.whyCN: 金融领域的配售保留了抽签分配的味道。

senses.title: A soldier's pay assigned to family
senses.definition: a portion of a soldier's pay assigned to dependents
senses.definitionCN: 军人薪饷中划给家属的部分
senses.example: He sent a monthly allotment home.
senses.exampleCN: 他每月往家里汇津贴。
senses.why: A fixed share of income formally assigned to someone.
senses.whyCN: 收入中被正式指派给某人的固定份额。

senses.title: A time allotment in schedules
senses.definition: a fixed amount of time set aside for an activity
senses.definitionCN: 为某活动设定的固定时长
senses.example: The exam's time allotment is three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 考试时间配额为三小时。
senses.why: The share logic extends neatly to clock time.
senses.whyCN: 份额逻辑顺延到钟表时间上。

senses.title: The distribution principle itself
senses.definition: allotment as a principle or system of distributing limited resources
senses.definitionCN: 分配有限资源的配给原则或制度
senses.example: The tribe opposed the allotment system.
senses.exampleCN: 部落反对配给制度。
senses.why: A repeated act can be discussed as an abstract system.
senses.whyCN: 反复进行的动作可被抽象为一种制度来讨论。

intro.en: Allotment is allot plus the noun suffix -ment, formed in English in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: allotment 由 allot 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，十五世纪成形于英语。

items.en: Reconstructed *hluta-, "share by lot", behind lot.
items.cn: lot 背后的重构词形 *hluta-「抽签之份」。

items.en: hlot, the drawn object deciding shares.
items.cn: 古英语 hlot，定份额的抽签物。

items.en: allot formed from a- + lot.

items.en: -ment, borrowed via French from Latin -mentum.

items.cn: allotment 最初记录「分配」这一动作。

items.cn: 义项涵盖配额、英国租种地与拨地。

note.en: Allotment competes with allocation in formal use, and pairs historically with the draw of lots.
note.cn: 正式语体中 allotment 与 allocation 相竞争，历史上与抽签搭配。

normal.cn: 英式画面：城边一排排菜地。

normal.cn: 配对：allot → allotment，如 assign → assignment。

normal.en: History: land allotments to settlers and Native Americans.

abstract.cn: 一个写着你名字的信箱格，里面躺着固定数目的硬币。

definition_zh: 合金：把一种金属与另一种金属或非金属熔合而成的材料；也指掺混、降低成色以及由此引申的混合体
definition_en: a metal made by melting and mixing two or more elements, and the act of mixing metals or of debasing one by adding another
core_image: 熔炉里两种金属液汇合，颜色由亮红转为银白，冷却后的断面均匀一致
scene: 坩埚里铜液与锡液汇合，颜色由亮红转向银白，冷却后的断面看不出两种金属。An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
sceneCN: 这里指合金这种材料（第 1 个义项：两种以上元素熔合而成的金属材料）；句意为铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。

pos.zh: 合金（材料，可数或不可数）
掺混物；降低成色的成分（常用于比喻）
熔合（金属）；掺杂使降低成色

collocations.phrase: an alloy of copper and tin

derivatives.zh: alloy + -ed（分词形容词）→ 已成合金的，语义偏移为「掺了其他成分而不再纯净的」
alloy + -ing（动名词）→ 合金化，语义偏移为「向金属中有意加入元素的工序」
super-（超）+ alloy → 高温合金，语义偏移为「能在极端温度下保持强度的合金」
non-（非）+ alloy → 非合金的，语义偏移为「未加合金元素的纯金属」
alloy + steel（钢）→ 合金钢，语义偏移为「加入铬、镍等元素的钢」

senses.title: The material
senses.titleCN: 合金：熔合而成的金属材料
senses.definition: a metal produced by melting and mixing two or more elements so that they form one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上元素熔合、混合成一种材料的金属
senses.example: An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
senses.exampleCN: 铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。
senses.why: Melting lets different metals dissolve into one another; when the melt solidifies, the mixture behaves as a single material, which is why the result gets its own name.
senses.whyCN: 熔炼让不同金属彼此溶解；熔体凝固后，混合物作为一个整体表现，因此产物得到了自己的名称。

senses.title: One recipe
senses.titleCN: 一种配比：特定成分的合金
senses.definition: a particular combination of metals with a stated proportion
senses.definitionCN: 按一定比例配成的特定金属组合
senses.example: The bell is cast from an alloy with about a fifth tin.
senses.exampleCN: 这口钟用一种含锡约五分之一的合金铸成。
senses.why: Once the class exists, each recipe counts as one alloy, because proportions change hardness, colour and sound.
senses.whyCN: 类别义一旦成立，每一种配方就算一种合金，因为比例会改变硬度、颜色与声音。

senses.title: A debasing mixture
senses.titleCN: 掺杂降质：混入物与不纯
senses.definition: something mixed in that lowers the purity or value of a metal, and by extension any unwanted addition
senses.definitionCN: 混入后降低金属纯度或价值的东西，引申为任何不需要的掺杂
senses.example: The gold was accepted without alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 这批黄金被认定毫无掺杂。
senses.why: Adding a cheaper metal to a precious one was a way of cheating weight and value, so the word also carries the sense of a loss of purity.
senses.whyCN: 在贵金属里掺入便宜金属，是偷重量、偷成色的手段，因此这个词也带有「纯净度受损」的含义。

senses.title: To fuse metals
senses.titleCN: 动词：把金属熔合在一起
senses.definition: to melt two or more metals together into one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上金属熔成一种材料
senses.example: They alloy the copper with a little beryllium.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在铜里加入少量铍，熔成合金。
senses.why: The noun's process sense turns into a verb, naming the deliberate act of combining melts rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: 名词的过程义转为动词，命名的是有意把熔体合并的动作，而不是结果。

senses.title: To debase
senses.definition: to lower the quality of a metal by adding a cheaper one
senses.definitionCN: 加入较便宜的金属以降低成色
senses.example: The mint alloyed the silver to stretch the supply.
senses.exampleCN: 铸币厂在银里掺料，以拉长供应。
senses.why: The same verb covers honest metallurgy and dishonest coinage; context decides whether the mixing is a recipe or a fraud.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既指正当的冶金，也指不正当的铸币；语境决定这种混合是配方还是欺诈。

senses.title: The coinage sense
senses.titleCN: 货币成色：铸币中的合金比例
senses.definition: the proportion of base metal in a coin, as a historical standard of value
senses.definitionCN: 硬币中贱金属所占的比例，历史上作为价值标准
senses.example: The alloy of the coin was fixed by royal decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这种硬币的成色由王室法令规定。
senses.why: Coins were valued by their precious metal content, so the mixing ratio became a matter of law rather than of workshop choice.
senses.whyCN: 硬币的价值取决于贵金属含量，因此配比成了法律问题，而不是作坊选择。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语：合金制的、含合金的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object or material as made of or containing an alloy
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某物由合金制成或含有合金
senses.example: Alloy wheels are lighter than steel ones.
senses.exampleCN: 合金轮毂比钢制的轻。
senses.why: A material noun can modify another noun directly, so the same word labels wheels, steel and frames without any ending.
senses.whyCN: 材料名词可以直接修饰另一名词，因此同一个词不加词尾就能标记轮毂、钢与车架。

senses.title: A mixture of anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻：由不同成分构成的混合体
senses.definition: a figurative mixture of different qualities, styles or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：不同性质、风格或情感构成的混合
senses.example: Her optimism was an alloy of memory and stubbornness.
senses.exampleCN: 她的乐观是记忆与固执的混合体。
senses.why: If a metal can be improved or debased by mixing, then a character or a style can be described as a mixture in the same way, with the same hint of impurity.
senses.whyCN: 既然金属能靠混合而改良或降质，那么性格或风格也可以用同样的方式描述为混合物，并带有同样一丝「不纯」的暗示。

intro.en: Alloy comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to bind to'. The metallurgical sense is the older one; the figurative sense of a mixed or debased thing grows out of it.
intro.cn: alloy 来自一个意为「绑到……上」的拉丁动词。冶金义是较早的一层，混合或降质的比喻义由它生长出来。

items.en: Alligare combined ad- 'to' with ligare 'to bind', and meant to tie or attach something to something else. This derivation is generally accepted and is reflected in the modern spelling.
items.cn: alligare 由 ad-「向」与 ligare「绑」组合而成，意为把某物系到另一物上。这一派生是公认的，并在现代拼写中留下痕迹。

items.en: Old French aloier took the Latin verb and used it for combining metals; the noun aloi named the resulting mixture and passed into English as alloy.
items.cn: 古法语 aloier 承袭这个拉丁动词，并用它指把金属合在一起；名词 aloi 指所得的混合物，进入英语后成为 alloy。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in the language of mints and metal trades, where combining and debasing were practical everyday matters.
items.cn: 这个名词自十六世纪起见于英语，最早出现在铸币与金属行业的话语里，在那里合料与降质是日常实务。

items.en: Because adding a base metal lowers value, the word acquired the sense of an unwanted element mixed into anything, which produced the phrase 'without alloy' for something pure.
items.cn: 因为掺入贱金属会降低价值，这个词获得了「混入任何东西里的不想要成分」之义，并产生「毫无掺杂」这一表示纯净的说法。

items.en: Modern metallurgy uses alloy for any deliberate multi-element metal and for the corresponding verb, and the attributive form labels products such as alloy steel and alloy wheels.
items.cn: 现代冶金用 alloy 指任何有意配成的多元素金属，也指相应的动词；定语形式则标记合金钢、合金轮毂一类产品。

items.en: Dating and sense shift: the exact first English citation is not fixed, and the sense development from 'binding' to 'mixing metals' happened inside French rather than in Latin.
items.cn: 年代与语义转移：确切的英语首见书证没有定论，而从「绑定」到「混合金属」的语义发展发生在法语内部，不在拉丁语中。

note.en: Group one holds words whose shapes invite confusion; group two holds the real neighbouring materials and processes.
note.cn: 第一组是形态上容易混淆的词；第二组是真正相邻的材料与工艺。

entries.definition: To reduce fear or pain, from Old English alecgan 'to lay down'; it sounds like alloy but has a native origin.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻恐惧或疼痛，来自古英语 alecgan「放下」；它读起来像 alloy，但来源是本族的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between buildings, from Old French alee 'a going'; the ending differs and the sense is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间的窄通道，来自古法语 alee「行走」；词尾不同，意义也无关。

entries.definition: A state or person joined to another by agreement, from Latin alligare through French; it shares the root 'to bind' but means a partner, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 通过协议与他方联合的国家或个人，经法语来自拉丁 alligare；它与 alloy 共享「绑」的词根，但指的是伙伴，不是材料。

entries.definition: Made into an alloy, or mixed with something less pure; a form of the same word, not a separate metal.
entries.definitionCN: 被做成合金的，或掺了较不纯成分的；是同一个词的形式，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: An alloy in which mercury is the main component, and by extension any blend; it is a special kind of alloy, not a general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 以汞为主要成分的合金，引申为任何混合物；它是合金的一个特殊种类，不是一般同义词。

entries.definition: A specific copper-tin alloy; alloy is the general class to which bronze belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 特指铜锡合金；alloy 是 bronze 所属的总类。

entries.definition: A material made of distinct components that remain separate, such as fibres in resin; an alloy is chemically mixed, a composite is not.
entries.definitionCN: 由仍保持分离的组分构成的材料，如树脂中的纤维；合金是化学意义上的混合，复合材料不是。

entries.definition: Any mixture, often of things that stay distinguishable; an alloy specifically involves molten metals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何混合物，通常其中成分仍可分辨；合金则专指熔融金属的混合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb 'to bind', the mint's practical sense, and the real alloy names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词「绑」、铸币厂的实务义，以及真实存在的合金名称。

normal.en: The root is 'to bind': ad- plus ligare, so an alloy is metals tied together rather than merely stirred.
normal.cn: 词根是「绑」：ad- 加 ligare，因此合金是被绑在一起的金属，而不只是被搅在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives ally: an ally is bound to you by agreement, an alloy is bound into one material.
normal.cn: 同一词根也给出 ally：盟友靠协议与你绑定，合金则被绑成一种材料。

normal.en: The dishonest sense is old: mints alloyed silver to make more coins from the same weight.
normal.cn: 不诚实的义项很古老：铸币厂在银里掺料，用同样的重量造出更多硬币。

normal.en: The real named alloys are bronze and brass, copper with tin and copper with zinc.
normal.cn: 真实有专名的合金是青铜与黄铜：铜加锡、铜加锌。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the class and the purity: alloy steel, alloy wheel, without alloy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类别与纯度：合金钢、合金轮毂、毫无掺杂。

abstract.en: Picture two melts meeting in one crucible and coming out as a single colour that neither had before.
abstract.cn: 想象两种熔体在同一只坩埚里相遇，出来时是一种两者原本都没有的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose value is written into its recipe, so the workshop becomes a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的价值被写进它的配方，于是作坊变成了法庭。

abstract.en: Picture a character described as a mixture: the same word that debases metal now debases a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的性格被描述为混合物：同一个曾用来降低金属成色的词，如今在降低一种情感的纯度。

examples.en: The frame is made of a light alloy that resists corrosion.
examples.cn: 这个车架由一种耐腐蚀的轻合金制成。

examples.en: Their joy was real but not without alloy.
examples.cn: 他们的快乐是真的，但并非毫无掺杂。

examples.en: The smith alloyed the copper with tin until the colour matched.
examples.cn: 铁匠在铜里加锡，直到颜色对得上。

dict_mnemonic.text: alloy＝合金；记「ad 向 + ligare 绑，把两种金属绑成一种」。

root: 拉丁 alligare「绑到……上」（ad- + ligare「绑」），经古法语 aloier、aloi 进入英语；由「合料」引申出合金、掺杂与混合体诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one binding: the material, one recipe of it, a debasing addition, the verb of fusing, the verb of debasing, coinage standard, the attributive label, and a mixture of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「绑合」这一动作展开：材料本身、一种配比、降低成色的掺入、熔合的动词、降质的动词、铸币成色、定语标签，以及任何事物的混合体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two molten metals meet in a crucible and solidify as one uniform block.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种熔融金属在坩埚中相遇，凝固成一块均匀的整体。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: mixing by melting produces something that behaves as one metal.
branches.cn: 材料本身：熔融混合产生的材料，表现得像一种金属。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: each set of proportions is a countable alloy with its own properties.
branches.cn: 配比层：每一组成分比例都是可数的一种合金，各有自己的性能。

branches.en: THE LOSS OF PURITY: adding a cheaper metal debases value, and in coinage the ratio becomes law.
branches.cn: 纯净度的损失：掺入便宜金属会降低价值，在铸币中配比还成了法律。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the deliberate combining of melts.
branches.cn: 动作层：动词命名有意把熔体合并的行为。

branches.en: THE EXTENSIONS: a material used as a modifier, and any mixture of qualities in a person or style.
branches.cn: 延伸层：作修饰语的材料，以及人或风格中任何性质的混合。

intro.en: Alloy is a borrowed noun and verb; its endings are ordinary English, and it compounds with material words such as steel and wheel.
intro.cn: alloy 是借来的名词兼动词；它接的词尾都是普通英语词尾，也能与 steel、wheel 这类材料或物件词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alligare, from ad- and ligare, is the source; the related noun alligatio meant a binding, and the same root reached English again through ally.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁 alligare，由 ad- 与 ligare 构成；相关名词 alligatio 意为绑缚，同一词根又经 ally 再次进入英语。

items.structure: alloy (n., v.; from Old French aloi, from Latin alligare)

items.meaningCN: 混合而成的金属，以及混合金属

items.meaning: made into or containing an alloy

an alloy that keeps its strength at extreme heat
items.meaningCN: 在极端高温下仍保持强度的合金

items.exampleCN: 涡轮叶片由高温合金制成。

items.meaning: a wheel cast from a light alloy

items.meaningCN: 从合金中去除某一元素的过程
